summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, a transplanted pancreas and kidney, mechanical mitral valve, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for revascularization of a non-healing left lower extremity ulcer. She had previously developed pneumonia during a prior admission, delaying the procedure. This time, her pulmonary status had improved, and a chest X-ray showed resolution of the prior infiltrate. She underwent successful left popliteal artery stenting with restoration of blood flow. The procedure was uncomplicated, and her left foot remained warm with dopplerable pulses. Anticoagulation was managed with IV heparin and bridging to coumadin, with fresh frozen plasma given preoperatively due to elevated INR. She remained afebrile, with stable vital signs and no signs of infection. She was discharged to extended care on IV heparin, aspirin, and coumadin, with plans for vascular surgery follow-up in four weeks.
